note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer following recent PSA rise and prior biopsy findings.

The patient is a 74-year-old retired truck driver who presents for urological re-evaluation. He has a known diagnosis of prostate cancer, initially identified on biopsy. His PSA levels have risen from 1.4 ng/mL in April 2024 to 3.87 ng/mL in January 2025. He reports no urinary symptoms, with an IPSS score of 4/35. He is widowed and lives with his partner, with a long-time friend as his next of kin. He cycles approximately 20 km twice weekly and consumes about 4 units of alcohol per week. Recent appointments included routine podiatry care and a flu vaccination administered by the GP practice nurse. He has no recorded comorbidities and takes no regular medication.

Digital rectal examination reveals a normal prostate without palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination is unremarkable, with stable vital signs and no signs of systemic illness.
